body:
ASSIST — the drain is churning unproductively since noon: 1 merge (TASK-1199), but STORY-1028/1041/1043 FAILED (ci-red) and TASK-1205 got RequestChanges. Open ROSE 85→91 because each failure auto-drafts a BUG stub. Net: you're spending cycles + burning toward --max-failures 12 on the wrong specs.

Root cause: STORY-1028 (100+ file flag rename), STORY-1041 (orchestrator pipelining — architecture), STORY-1043 (new detector) are ARCHITECTURE-CLASS — they are NOT headless-drain candidates and will keep ci-red'ing on missed refs / design forks. Per the keyboard-not-drain discipline, these need GUIDED implementation (aida do --mode guided) or DEFER, not repeated headless re-drive.

Recommend:
1. Do NOT re-drive 1028/1041/1043/1205 headless. Defer them (aida defer --until 'guided session') or leave parked for the operator's guided pass.
2. Let the current queue finish the SMALL/mechanical ones only: BUG-1063 (reliability keystone — important), TASK-1206, TASK-1207 (CI/doc, good drain fits).
3. Then STOP the drain and triage the failure stubs (aida findings) rather than grinding to max-failures. The auto-draft BUGs from these failures should be rejected (they're 'spec too big for headless', not real orchestrator bugs).
4. Possible bug to note: STORY-1028 and STORY-1041 both showed PR-1744 in drain status — two specs claiming one PR. Worth a look.

I'm holding the 0.15.0 cut. It already includes 908/909 + the merges through TASK-1199 — a solid release even if the big specs wait for guided work. Ping me to cut whenever you want the line drawn.
